title: Lettre Tate (mai 66) (Cristaux) : lettre (1966), tapuscrit (s.d.), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is a faint carbon or typescript copy of the opening of Grothendieck's May 1966 letter to John Tate from Pisa. It duplicates the previous page.

Setting. Fix a morphism of preschemes S -> R; the main case is R = Spec Z.

The category C. Its objects are R-preschemes T equipped with an R-morphism S -> T that is a closed immersion defined by a locally nilpotent ideal. These are the nilpotent thickenings of S, with no retraction T -> S required and no divided-power structure. Restricting the fibered category of quasi-coherent modules along the forgetful functor C -> (Sch) gives a fibered category over C, T |-> QCoh(T).

Definition 1.1. A crystal of (quasi-coherent) modules on S relative to R is a cartesian section of this fibered category over C. Concretely it is:
- a family of quasi-coherent modules M_T, one for each thickening T;
- for each morphism u: T' -> T in C, an isomorphism u^*M_T ≅ M_{T'};
- these isomorphisms satisfy the cocycle conditions.
For any fibered category F over (Sch)/R, an F-crystal is defined the same way: a cartesian section of F restricted to C. This covers crystals of algebras, of commutative algebras, of relative schemes, and so on. When R = Spec Z the crystal is called 'absolu'.

1.2. F-crystals form a category depending functorially on F. Applied to the module case, this transports the usual tensor operations (tensor product, etc.) to crystals of modules, with their usual properties.

Purpose. This is the founding definition of crystalline cohomology. The aim is to give a characteristic-free, rigid replacement for de Rham cohomology and to encode Dieudonné-type invariants of formal groups. Tate's p-divisible groups and formal groups are the motivation stated in the first line.

Modern reading. C is (the underlying category of) the absolute or relative infinitesimal site Inf(S/R), here without a topology, using global thickenings. A crystal of modules is a crystal in quasi-coherent modules on this site.
errors: No mathematical error, but there is a known gap that Grothendieck himself later corrected. Without divided powers, the nilpotent-thickening site gives the wrong cohomology in characteristic p. The infinitesimal topos computes de Rham cohomology only in characteristic 0. Grothendieck soon recognised this; Berthelot carried out the PD (crystalline) site, which is the standard theory.

Size and localization are not addressed. C is not small, and no Zariski or étale localization of thickenings is imposed. These are harmless here, since quasi-coherent modules satisfy descent and crystals defined with global thickenings agree with those on the site.
The image appears to read 'cristaux de modules sur C'; this should be 'sur S'. It is a slip on the copy, as the previous page has 'sur S'.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a copy of the well-known opening of the 1966 letter to Tate introducing crystals. The definition of crystals over nilpotent thickenings, and of F-crystals for general fibered categories, is the standard and published origin of crystalline cohomology, widely cited.
transcription_corrections: This page is a duplicate (carbon or typescript copy) of page 1; the text is identical apart from typographic variants.
Heading 'Chapitre I' / 'Chapitre 1': the image shows an underlined 'Chapitre 1.'
'De Rham' in the transcription: the original typescript likely reads 'De Rahm', as on the previous page.
'R-préschémas': the 'R-' is a handwritten insertion above 'préschémas', and 'T' is inserted after 'préschémas'.
'R-[-m-]morphisme': the image shows 'R-mmorphisme' with a typed overstrike, i.e. 'R-morphisme'.
'sur la catégorie des cristaux de modules sur C': should read 'sur S' (as on page 1); the carbon is ambiguous.
'souffre' is Grothendieck's spelling (for 'soufre') and should be kept as is.
